title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to the cote-142 notes. The previous page set up the projective line Σ_J = P(V(J)) for a 3-element set J, with its distinguished points R_i, Q_i and P_ω and the sections φ_jk. The next page has a torus picture and a 12-gon. This page is a short side study of the 'dihedral' regular maps.

The map. Σ_n is the oriented regular map on the sphere given by a regular n-gon P_n (n ≥ 2). It has two faces (centres 0 and ∞), n vertices and n edges. In a model on P^1, put the vertices at μ_n and the edge midpoints at the other 2n-th roots of unity. Σ_n^{**·} denotes Σ_n minus its vertices, edge midpoints and face centres, i.e. Σ_n minus (S ∪ A ∪ F). It equals P^1 minus {0, ∞, μ_{2n}}.

The first tower. The orientation-preserving automorphism group is D_n^+ (dihedral of order 2n: rotations, plus the flips that swap the two faces). The full group D_n (order 4n) also contains reflections, with D_n/D_n^+ = Z/2.
- z ↦ z^n is a cyclic cover of degree n from Σ_n^{**·} onto Σ_1^{**·} = P^1 minus {0, ∞, 1, −1}. Here 0, ∞ are the 'pôles' (face centres), 1 is the vertex and −1 is the edge midpoint of the 1-gon.
- A further degree-2 map takes this to U_{0,3}, the projective line minus 3 points. It can be z ↦ z^2, or the quotient by z ↦ 1/z.
- So Σ_n^{**·}/D_n^+ is a degree-2n cover of U_{0,3} (by the quotient-map ordering I read the target as Σ_n^{**·}/D_n^+ = U_{0,3}, the (2,2,n) triangle quotient). The page also writes the equality Σ_1^{**·} = Σ_n^{**·}/D_n, reading as given but not verified.

The key remark. Σ_n^{**·} ≅ Σ_{2n}^{**}: subdividing each edge at its midpoint turns the n-gon map into the 2n-gon map, now removing only vertices and face centres. This gives a second tower:
- Σ_{2n}^{**} → Σ_2^{**} (= P^1 minus {0, ∞, ±1}) → Σ_1^{**} = P^1 minus {0, ∞, 1} = U_0^3, by z^n followed by z^2. This is 'division par D_{2n}^+'.
- Hence the larger group D_{2n} ⊃ D_n acts on the same punctured sphere.

The diagram. This produces the lattice of intermediate quotients drawn on the page:
- Σ_n^{**·} ≅ Σ_{2n}^{**};
- its quotients by D_n^+, D_{2n}^+, D_n, D_{2n};
- with identifications Σ_n^{**·}/D_n^+ ≅ Σ_1^{**·} ≅ Σ_2^{**}, and final quotient Σ/D_{2n}.

The last remark. Dividing by the full D_n, including reflections, gives non-orientable / bordered quotients: orbifolds with reflector edges ('réflexion sur ces arêtes').

Purpose. The point is to place the dihedral dessins z^n inside the Galois/Teichmüller programme, as the genus-0 regular maps attached to the triangle (2,2,n). They are bookkeeping for the configurations of special points R_i, Q_i, P_ω on Σ_J used on the neighbouring pages.
errors: The first line's target 'Σ_3^{*·} = U_{03}' is most plausibly Σ_1^{*·} (or a mis-transcribed index). A degree-2 quotient of P^1 minus {0, ∞, ±1} is P^1 minus three points, and the next line has the parallel Σ_1^{**} ≃ U_0^3.

The superscript notation (*, *, ·) for which strata are removed is used inconsistently. Some quotients in the diagram (e.g. Σ_n^{**}/D_n written as Σ_1^{**}) depend on which strata are deleted and are only sketched.
Quotients by groups containing reflections (D_n, D_{2n}) are not Riemann surfaces but surfaces with boundary / reflector orbifolds. Grothendieck notes this only at the end.

ideas.what: Dihedral regular maps on the sphere (regular n-gon with two faces) and their Belyi maps z^n, with automorphism group D_n^+ and quotient the (2,2,n) triangle orbifold
ideas.modern_name: dihedral dessins d'enfants / regular maps of type {n,2}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein; regular maps Coxeter–Moser); dessins: Grothendieck, Jones–Singerman, Wolfart
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps and polyhedra in general, not this dihedral computation specifically

ideas.what: Removing edge midpoints of the n-gon map gives the 2n-gon map with vertices and faces removed (barycentric/edge subdivision), so D_{2n} acts and gives a lattice of intermediate quotients
ideas.modern_name: edge subdivision of dessins; normalizer / tower of covers of P^1 minus 3 or 4 points

ideas.what: Quotient by orientation-reversing automorphisms gives surfaces with reflecting edges
ideas.modern_name: non-orientable / bordered orbifold quotients; real structures on dessins

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine computations with dihedral regular maps and their quotient lattice, all classical in the theory of dessins. The page is useful only as working notes linking to the Σ_J / torus configuration on the adjacent pages.
transcription_corrections: 'Σ_n^{**}' in many places should carry three marks (Σ_n^{**·}: vertices, face centres and edge midpoints removed), as in the defining line.
'revêtement [?] par D_n^+ ⊂ D_{2n}^+' — the image reads roughly 'revêtement par D_n^+ ⊂ D_{2n}^+'.
The left-margin lines read approximately '(on n'a enlevé que les sommets et centres faces)' and 'À cause de tout ceci, on a joint ... D_{2n} opérant sur Σ_n^{**·} (≃ Σ_{2n}^{**}), on trouve'.
The final note reads approximately 'Si on divise par D_n tout entier, on trouve des [surfaces] à réflexion sur ces arêtes'.
'Σ_3^{*·} = U_{03}' likely 'Σ_1^{*·} = U_{03}'; the right margin '(cartes régulières Σ_α à … sommets)'.
